bull_bear.body:
- Regulated Delhi distribution utilities serving a large consumer base described by the Company as providing stable and predictable cash flows
- Transmission and distribution losses comparable to international benchmarks - BRPL at 6.31% and BYPL at 6.40% in Financial Year 2025-26
- System availability maintained at over 99.9% at both Delhi Discoms, with peak demand of 3,803 MW met by BRPL and 1,824 MW by BYPL
- Highest 'A+' grade in the Consumer Service Rating of DISCOMs (CSRD) conducted by REC Limited among 66 Discoms evaluated for Financial Year 2024-25
- Mumbai Metro Line-1 is described as the busiest metro corridor in India, having served over 1200 million passengers as of March 31, 2026, with interchanges at Ghatkopar and Andheri connecting to the suburban rail network
- Defence business built on strategic partnerships with Dassault Aviation, Thales and Diehl Defence, with over 1,241 assemblies delivered and pioneering indigenisation of critical radar components
- Integrated business model delivering end-to-end solutions from project development and execution through to operations and maintenance
- Diversified portfolio of stable core assets alongside emerging growth platforms in defence and clean energy
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Tariff and regulatory risk in the power distribution business — Consumer tariffs for electricity distribution are regulated by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions, and for the Delhi Discoms by DERC; any adverse changes in the tariff structure or delays in tariff approvals could impact the financial performance of the Delhi Discoms. The sector also faces high subsidy dependence, delayed tariff revisions and legacy infrastructure constraints that continue to impact Discoms' financial health.
- Single-activity revenue concentration in power distribution — The BRSR discloses that the Power Distribution Business accounts for 91.53% of the entity's turnover, so the diversified infrastructure portfolio is in practice dependent on one regulated activity; exports contribute only 1.90% of total turnover.
- Defence sector structural and procurement risk — The defence sector is characterised by long developmental periods, high capital investment requirements and strong reliance on government procurement, with extensive regulatory compliance for setting up and operating facilities and for manufacture and sale; global competition, evolving geopolitical dynamics, extended procurement cycles and competitive intensity from PSUs and international players can impact timelines, margins and scalability.
- Mumbai Metro capacity constraints and fare revision delays — Capacity constraints may limit the ability to fully cater to growing ridership, and delays in fare revisions over the past twelve years have constrained the availability of funds required for capacity augmentation and infrastructure upgrades, which could impact operational efficiency and service quality over time.
- Shrinking roads portfolio and traffic-linked toll revenue — The gradual reduction in the size of the roads portfolio may lead to moderation in revenues over time; toll road revenues remain linked to traffic volumes and may be affected by economic conditions, fuel prices and unforeseen external disruptions, impacting toll collections and project returns.
- E&C order book depletion — Most of the existing E&C projects are either nearing completion or have already been completed, leaving the Division dependent on strengthening its pipeline through selective and strategic bidding.
- Financial risk - project cash flows versus debt service — Financial risk is the risk that project cash flows might be insufficient to cover debt service and then pay an adequate return on sponsor equity; substantial government risk sharing through viability gap funding, revenue or debt guarantees, or participation by state or multilateral development institutions is required.
- Legal and operating risk in a highly regulated environment — Changes in applicable laws, contractual disputes, delays in arbitration outcomes or weak enforcement of contractual provisions may adversely affect project returns; various regulatory actions were initiated against the Company and its subsidiaries during the year. Operating risks include project execution challenges, system failures and external disruptions such as natural disasters, industrial disturbances or geopolitical developments.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Reliance Infrastructure Limited is a diversified infrastructure company with capabilities across Engineering & Construction (E&C), power utilities, transportation and emerging segments such as defence and renewable energy, operating an integrated business model that delivers end-to-end solutions from project development and execution to operations and maintenance. Its core portfolio is power distribution through the Delhi Discoms (BSES Rajdhani Power Limited and BSES Yamuna Power Limited), urban mobility through Mumbai Metro Line-1 built on a build-own-operate-transfer basis, and toll road assets in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. It also executes EPC projects for government and semi-government agencies and, through its defence business, serves domestic and international defence and aerospace customers via partnerships with Dassault Aviation, Thales and Diehl Defence.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Power Distribution:** Electricity distribution in licensed areas of the National Capital Territory of Delhi through BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL), Electricity distribution in licensed areas of the National Capital Territory of Delhi through BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL)
- **Urban Mobility / Metro:** Mumbai Metro Line-1 on the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor, operated by Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (MMOPL)
- **Roads:** Toll roads - 10 toll plazas operating on 6 toll roads across Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu (Pune-Satara, Dindigul-Samayanallore, Salem-Ulundurpet, Trichy-Karur, Trichy-Dindigul, Namakkal-Karur)
- **Engineering & Construction (E&C):** EPC projects for government and semi-government agencies such as NHAI, NPCIL and MSRDC
- **Defence:** Aerostructures and assemblies for the Falcon 2000, Falcon 6X, Falcon 8X and Rafale platforms (through Dassault Reliance Aerospace Limited), Assembly and integration of AESA radars, electronic warfare suites and navigation equipment for the Rafale fleet (through Thales Reliance Defence Systems), New generation 155 mm artillery shells designed and developed with ARDE, Pune (a DRDO laboratory)
- **Clean energy (emerging):** Solar, Battery storage

outlook.body:
- Strategic expansion into defence manufacturing and clean energy solutions, including solar and battery storage, aligned with national priorities of infrastructure development, energy transition and self-reliance
- Continued focus on balance sheet strengthening, disciplined capital allocation and asset monetisation to enhance financial flexibility and support future investments
- Leverage the diversified portfolio of stable core assets in power distribution, urban mobility and transportation infrastructure for steady cash flows and operational stability
- In E&C, focus on efficient execution of the current order book and strengthen the pipeline through selective and strategic bidding, with emphasis on value engineering to enhance competitiveness
- In Mumbai Metro, strengthen last mile access by collaborating with bus services and aligning timetables with other public transport modes
- In Mumbai Metro, adopt digital ticketing and interoperable payments (NCMC, One Ticket and Mumbai One) for seamless travel across transit systems
- Risk management through a defined Risk Management Policy applicable to all businesses, with quarterly independent review of major risks by the Board's Risk Management Committee
- The routed governance text sets out no dividend or payout philosophy. It records that during the financial year under review the Company did not transfer any amounts to reserves, did not issue any equity shares with differential rights as to dividend or voting or any sweat equity shares to Directors or Employees, did not change its nature of business, and did not enter into any agreement for one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution. It also discloses that on an application under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 filed by a creditor, the NCLT admitted the Company into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process by order dated May 30, 2025; the Company, having already made full payment of the entire amount claimed by the creditors, appealed to the NCLAT, which suspended the order on June 4, 2025 and stayed the order and the CIRP on July 18, 2025, with the matter currently pending. In a separate matter disposed of by the NCLT on August 21, 2025 following settlement, the operational creditor has filed a restoration application which is pending. Under related-party disclosures, parties where control exists: none.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed text describes expansion mainly in the Delhi power distribution business and through new entity formation rather than as a named capex programme. Capital expenditure at the Delhi Discoms during Financial Year 2025-26 stood at Rs. 1,579 crore, directed towards upgradation, strengthening, reliability improvement and modernisation of the power distribution infrastructure, while the customer base grew by over 4.19% during the year and system availability was maintained at over 99.9%. Beyond its established businesses the Company states it is proposing to strategically expand into high-growth areas such as defence manufacturing and clean energy solutions, including solar and battery storage, in alignment with national priorities. On the entity side, during the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned foreign subsidiary, SB Holding L.L.C-FZ in Dubai, and its associate Reliance Enterprises Private Limited formed a joint venture, GDL - Reliance Solar Pte Ltd in Bhutan, with Green Digital Private Limited, a State Owned Enterprise of the Royal Government of Bhutan. For Mumbai Metro, the growth narrative is the expansion of the wider Mumbai metro network (operational Lines 2A, 7 and 3, partially opened Lines 2B and 9, and upcoming Line 4), which is expected to cross-feed ridership onto the Company's Line-1 rather than being the Company's own capex; the Company also flags that delays in fare revisions over the past twelve years have constrained funds required for capacity augmentation and infrastructure upgrades. No new plant, line or project commissioning timeline for the Company itself is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Power distribution: sector transformation driven by policy reforms, technological integration and service reliability focus, with RDSS and regulatory focus on reducing AT&C losses reshaping industry structure, and a shift towards digitalisation, smart metering and consumer-centric models
- Power distribution headwinds: high subsidy dependence, delayed tariff revisions and legacy infrastructure constraints continue to impact Discoms' financial health
- Defence: sustained policy emphasis on indigenisation and self-reliance (Defence Acquisition Procedure, Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan), progressive FDI liberalisation and a steadily increasing defence budget creating opportunities for private participation, with long-term visibility from multi-year procurement programmes and collaboration with global OEMs
- Defence headwinds: extended procurement cycles, evolving regulatory requirements and competitive intensity from PSUs and international players
- Mumbai Metro: expansion of the metro network (operational Lines 2A, 7 and 3, partially opened Lines 2B and 9, and upcoming Line 4) is expected to enhance connectivity and cross-feed ridership, leading to increased commuter volumes
- Roads: India's road sector is poised for strong growth backed by rising vehicular traffic, with record-high vehicle sales in Financial Year 2025-26 indicating a positive outlook for passenger traffic on highways
- Roads policy support: the Government of India target to construct 10,000 km of highways in Financial Year 2026-27 and plans to raise 30,000 crore through road asset monetisation are described as creating strong tailwinds for the sector
- Roads technology: NHAI's GNSS-based Electronic Toll Collection, integrating with FASTag under a hybrid model and eventually eliminating toll plazas, is expected to reduce operational and maintenance costs for toll road operators and enhance profitability
- Roads threat: construction of parallel roads may pose a competitive threat, though economic growth and vehicle sales momentum are expected to sustain and grow traffic volumes on the Company's road assets
- E&C: most of the existing projects are either nearing completion or have already been completed; the Division remains focused on efficient execution of its current order book
- E&C: aims to strengthen its pipeline through selective and strategic bidding opportunities, with emphasis on value engineering to enhance competitiveness

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Reliance Infrastructure Limited is a diversified infrastructure company with capabilities across Engineering & Construction (E&C), power utilities, transportation and emerging segments such as defence and renewable energy, operating an integrated business model that delivers end-to-end solutions from project development and execution to operations and maintenance. Its core portfolio is power distribution through the Delhi Discoms (BSES Rajdhani Power Limited and BSES Yamuna Power Limited), urban mobility through Mumbai Metro Line-1 built on a build-own-operate-transfer basis, and toll road assets in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. It also executes EPC projects for government and semi-government agencies and, through its defence business, serves domestic and international defence and aerospace customers via partnerships with Dassault Aviation, Thales and Diehl Defence.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Power Distribution:** Electricity distribution in licensed areas of the National Capital Territory of Delhi through BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL), Electricity distribution in licensed areas of the National Capital Territory of Delhi through BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL)
- **Urban Mobility / Metro:** Mumbai Metro Line-1 on the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor, operated by Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (MMOPL)
- **Roads:** Toll roads - 10 toll plazas operating on 6 toll roads across Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu (Pune-Satara, Dindigul-Samayanallore, Salem-Ulundurpet, Trichy-Karur, Trichy-Dindigul, Namakkal-Karur)
- **Engineering & Construction (E&C):** EPC projects for government and semi-government agencies such as NHAI, NPCIL and MSRDC
- **Defence:** Aerostructures and assemblies for the Falcon 2000, Falcon 6X, Falcon 8X and Rafale platforms (through Dassault Reliance Aerospace Limited), Assembly and integration of AESA radars, electronic warfare suites and navigation equipment for the Rafale fleet (through Thales Reliance Defence Systems), New generation 155 mm artillery shells designed and developed with ARDE, Pune (a DRDO laboratory)
- **Clean energy (emerging):** Solar, Battery storage

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Power distribution: sector transformation driven by policy reforms, technological integration and service reliability focus, with RDSS and regulatory focus on reducing AT&C losses reshaping industry structure, and a shift towards digitalisation, smart metering and consumer-centric models
- Power distribution headwinds: high subsidy dependence, delayed tariff revisions and legacy infrastructure constraints continue to impact Discoms' financial health
- Defence: sustained policy emphasis on indigenisation and self-reliance (Defence Acquisition Procedure, Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan), progressive FDI liberalisation and a steadily increasing defence budget creating opportunities for private participation, with long-term visibility from multi-year procurement programmes and collaboration with global OEMs
- Defence headwinds: extended procurement cycles, evolving regulatory requirements and competitive intensity from PSUs and international players
- Mumbai Metro: expansion of the metro network (operational Lines 2A, 7 and 3, partially opened Lines 2B and 9, and upcoming Line 4) is expected to enhance connectivity and cross-feed ridership, leading to increased commuter volumes
- Roads: India's road sector is poised for strong growth backed by rising vehicular traffic, with record-high vehicle sales in Financial Year 2025-26 indicating a positive outlook for passenger traffic on highways
- Roads policy support: the Government of India target to construct 10,000 km of highways in Financial Year 2026-27 and plans to raise 30,000 crore through road asset monetisation are described as creating strong tailwinds for the sector
- Roads technology: NHAI's GNSS-based Electronic Toll Collection, integrating with FASTag under a hybrid model and eventually eliminating toll plazas, is expected to reduce operational and maintenance costs for toll road operators and enhance profitability
- Roads threat: construction of parallel roads may pose a competitive threat, though economic growth and vehicle sales momentum are expected to sustain and grow traffic volumes on the Company's road assets
- E&C: most of the existing projects are either nearing completion or have already been completed; the Division remains focused on efficient execution of its current order book
- E&C: aims to strengthen its pipeline through selective and strategic bidding opportunities, with emphasis on value engineering to enhance competitiveness

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strategic expansion into defence manufacturing and clean energy solutions, including solar and battery storage, aligned with national priorities of infrastructure development, energy transition and self-reliance
- Continued focus on balance sheet strengthening, disciplined capital allocation and asset monetisation to enhance financial flexibility and support future investments
- Leverage the diversified portfolio of stable core assets in power distribution, urban mobility and transportation infrastructure for steady cash flows and operational stability
- In E&C, focus on efficient execution of the current order book and strengthen the pipeline through selective and strategic bidding, with emphasis on value engineering to enhance competitiveness
- In Mumbai Metro, strengthen last mile access by collaborating with bus services and aligning timetables with other public transport modes
- In Mumbai Metro, adopt digital ticketing and interoperable payments (NCMC, One Ticket and Mumbai One) for seamless travel across transit systems
- Risk management through a defined Risk Management Policy applicable to all businesses, with quarterly independent review of major risks by the Board's Risk Management Committee
- The routed governance text sets out no dividend or payout philosophy. It records that during the financial year under review the Company did not transfer any amounts to reserves, did not issue any equity shares with differential rights as to dividend or voting or any sweat equity shares to Directors or Employees, did not change its nature of business, and did not enter into any agreement for one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution. It also discloses that on an application under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 filed by a creditor, the NCLT admitted the Company into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process by order dated May 30, 2025; the Company, having already made full payment of the entire amount claimed by the creditors, appealed to the NCLAT, which suspended the order on June 4, 2025 and stayed the order and the CIRP on July 18, 2025, with the matter currently pending. In a separate matter disposed of by the NCLT on August 21, 2025 following settlement, the operational creditor has filed a restoration application which is pending. Under related-party disclosures, parties where control exists: none.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed text describes expansion mainly in the Delhi power distribution business and through new entity formation rather than as a named capex programme. Capital expenditure at the Delhi Discoms during Financial Year 2025-26 stood at Rs. 1,579 crore, directed towards upgradation, strengthening, reliability improvement and modernisation of the power distribution infrastructure, while the customer base grew by over 4.19% during the year and system availability was maintained at over 99.9%. Beyond its established businesses the Company states it is proposing to strategically expand into high-growth areas such as defence manufacturing and clean energy solutions, including solar and battery storage, in alignment with national priorities. On the entity side, during the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned foreign subsidiary, SB Holding L.L.C-FZ in Dubai, and its associate Reliance Enterprises Private Limited formed a joint venture, GDL - Reliance Solar Pte Ltd in Bhutan, with Green Digital Private Limited, a State Owned Enterprise of the Royal Government of Bhutan. For Mumbai Metro, the growth narrative is the expansion of the wider Mumbai metro network (operational Lines 2A, 7 and 3, partially opened Lines 2B and 9, and upcoming Line 4), which is expected to cross-feed ridership onto the Company's Line-1 rather than being the Company's own capex; the Company also flags that delays in fare revisions over the past twelve years have constrained funds required for capacity augmentation and infrastructure upgrades. No new plant, line or project commissioning timeline for the Company itself is disclosed in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Regulated Delhi distribution utilities serving a large consumer base described by the Company as providing stable and predictable cash flows
- Transmission and distribution losses comparable to international benchmarks - BRPL at 6.31% and BYPL at 6.40% in Financial Year 2025-26
- System availability maintained at over 99.9% at both Delhi Discoms, with peak demand of 3,803 MW met by BRPL and 1,824 MW by BYPL
- Highest 'A+' grade in the Consumer Service Rating of DISCOMs (CSRD) conducted by REC Limited among 66 Discoms evaluated for Financial Year 2024-25
- Mumbai Metro Line-1 is described as the busiest metro corridor in India, having served over 1200 million passengers as of March 31, 2026, with interchanges at Ghatkopar and Andheri connecting to the suburban rail network
- Defence business built on strategic partnerships with Dassault Aviation, Thales and Diehl Defence, with over 1,241 assemblies delivered and pioneering indigenisation of critical radar components
- Integrated business model delivering end-to-end solutions from project development and execution through to operations and maintenance
- Diversified portfolio of stable core assets alongside emerging growth platforms in defence and clean energy

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Tariff and regulatory risk in the power distribution business — Consumer tariffs for electricity distribution are regulated by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions, and for the Delhi Discoms by DERC; any adverse changes in the tariff structure or delays in tariff approvals could impact the financial performance of the Delhi Discoms. The sector also faces high subsidy dependence, delayed tariff revisions and legacy infrastructure constraints that continue to impact Discoms' financial health.
- Single-activity revenue concentration in power distribution — The BRSR discloses that the Power Distribution Business accounts for 91.53% of the entity's turnover, so the diversified infrastructure portfolio is in practice dependent on one regulated activity; exports contribute only 1.90% of total turnover.
- Defence sector structural and procurement risk — The defence sector is characterised by long developmental periods, high capital investment requirements and strong reliance on government procurement, with extensive regulatory compliance for setting up and operating facilities and for manufacture and sale; global competition, evolving geopolitical dynamics, extended procurement cycles and competitive intensity from PSUs and international players can impact timelines, margins and scalability.
- Mumbai Metro capacity constraints and fare revision delays — Capacity constraints may limit the ability to fully cater to growing ridership, and delays in fare revisions over the past twelve years have constrained the availability of funds required for capacity augmentation and infrastructure upgrades, which could impact operational efficiency and service quality over time.
- Shrinking roads portfolio and traffic-linked toll revenue — The gradual reduction in the size of the roads portfolio may lead to moderation in revenues over time; toll road revenues remain linked to traffic volumes and may be affected by economic conditions, fuel prices and unforeseen external disruptions, impacting toll collections and project returns.
- E&C order book depletion — Most of the existing E&C projects are either nearing completion or have already been completed, leaving the Division dependent on strengthening its pipeline through selective and strategic bidding.
- Financial risk - project cash flows versus debt service — Financial risk is the risk that project cash flows might be insufficient to cover debt service and then pay an adequate return on sponsor equity; substantial government risk sharing through viability gap funding, revenue or debt guarantees, or participation by state or multilateral development institutions is required.
- Legal and operating risk in a highly regulated environment — Changes in applicable laws, contractual disputes, delays in arbitration outcomes or weak enforcement of contractual provisions may adversely affect project returns; various regulatory actions were initiated against the Company and its subsidiaries during the year. Operating risks include project execution challenges, system failures and external disruptions such as natural disasters, industrial disturbances or geopolitical developments.
